title: Modern Manufacturing at nVent: How Continuous Improvement Powers our Commitment to Safety, Sustainability, and Excellence
body_markdown:
NEWS ARTICLE


Modern Manufacturing at nVent: How Continuous Improvement Powers our Commitment to Safety, Sustainability, and Excellence


*By Mellinda Devese, Chief Supply Chain Officer*


For those who have never stepped inside a manufacturing facility, they may picture rows of machines and repetitive tasks. The reality is something very different. Modern manufacturing is driven by innovation, technology, problem-solving and talented people who are continuously finding better ways to serve customers, improve safety and reduce our environmental impact.


Each year,[Manufacturing Day](https://mfgday.com/) gives us an opportunity to showcase what modern manufacturing looks like.


At nVent, manufacturing is more than making products. It is how we bring our purpose to life. Every day, our teams manufacture solutions that connect and protect critical electrical infrastructure that powers data centers, utilities, renewable energy projects, commercial buildings and industrial facilities around the world. We are helping build a more sustainable and electrified future.


As I have traveled across our global manufacturing centers this year, one theme has stood out everywhere I go: a relentless commitment to continuous improvement.


I have seen teams simplify processes, eliminate waste, improve quality, strengthen safety practices and find innovative ways to serve customers better. These efforts may look different from site to site, but they are all grounded in the same belief: excellence is never finished. There is always an opportunity to learn, improve and raise the bar.


That mindset is embedded in the nVent Spark Management System and our Lean Enterprise approach, which focuses on eliminating waste, increasing velocity and empowering employees to solve problems closest to where the work happens.


Safety is one of the clearest examples of this continuous improvement culture in action. Across nVent, teams are implementing new tools, sharing best practices and strengthening our safety culture through programs such as Safety Dojos, immersive training environments that help employees build critical safety knowledge before entering the production floor. In 2025, we expanded Safety Dojos across most of our manufacturing and distribution sites and are working toward implementing them across all facilities.


The same commitment to continuous improvement is helping us advance our sustainability journey. Sustainability is not a separate initiative at nVent. It is integrated into how we design products, operate facilities and make decisions across our value chain. We believe responsible manufacturing and business performance go hand in hand.


In 2025, we reduced Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 10% compared to our 2024 baseline and decreased water use in high water-risk areas by 9%. We also reduced overall water consumption by 8% and continued investing in renewable energy, operational efficiency and waste reduction initiatives across our facilities. In 2025, we reduced normalized energy consumption by 15% year over year through more efficient equipment, modernized systems, and better use of submetering data to identify and address energy spikes.


Some of our most impactful improvements come from employees identifying opportunities in their own workplaces. Across our global sites, teams generated more than 100 environmental improvement ideas through our environmental assessment process, leading to projects that reduce energy use, conserve water and minimize waste.


Manufacturing excellence also means continuously improving the products we deliver to customers. As demand grows for more reliable electrical infrastructure, renewable energy and AI-enabled data centers, our teams are innovating solutions that improve efficiency, resiliency and safety. We recently established a life cycle assessment model to better understand and reduce the environmental impact of our products, while also expanding efforts to eliminate single-use plastics and foams from product packaging.


**None of this happens without our people** .


The foundation of modern manufacturing is skilled employees who embrace challenges, solve problems and work together to improve every day. Whether they are operating equipment, engineering new technologies, managing supply chains or leading continuous improvement efforts, our people are the reason we continue to make progress.


There are millions of new modern manufacturing jobs coming online in the next decade. Manufacturing Day provides an opportunity for students, educators, families and communities to see firsthand how dynamic, innovative and purpose-driven today's manufacturing environment has become. Manufacturing careers offer opportunities to learn, grow and make a meaningful impact. They also play a critical role in solving some of society's biggest challenges, from expanding electrical infrastructure to supporting sustainability and accelerating innovation.


The future of manufacturing is being shaped right now by the people who show up each day ready to learn, improve and solve problems.


Based on what I have seen firsthand across nVent, that future is incredibly bright.
